title: Filipino Garlic-Bay Adobo Pan Sauce
description: Whole softened garlic, bay and cider vinegar give this Filipino-style adobo sauce a savory, gently puckering finish.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

steps.title: Soften the cloves
steps.text: Keep {ga} whole and simmer with {ch} and {bay} under a lid for 7–9 minutes until the cloves mash easily.

steps.title: Mellow the vinegar
steps.text: Add {cv}, {a}, {pep} and {bs}. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes to soften the sharp edge.

steps.title: Smooth the garlic
steps.text: Take off the heat and blend the soft garlic into the liquid. Return the smooth base to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over braised chicken thighs or pork and steamed rice. A little extra black pepper can go on individual plates.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 5 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, use 2 teaspoons cider vinegar, omit the pepper and use half the garlic. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 25 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 5.3 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 122 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 20 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 4.0 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 32 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
